title: View of stairs and oak tree from balcony
Brahea 'Clara' palm with bromeliads and Restios at 28 Vallejo St
description: One of the most beautiful drought and cold tolerant palms for a northern California garden.  This Brahea is too little seen in local gardens, yet has such grace and charm, a stunning accent palm for almost any garden.  It is faster to get height than the similar looking Brahea armata, with larger foliage and ultimately taller growing.  It works as well as an accent shrub while younger, used here as a privacy screen from the neighbors, or a tall palm in the landscape with time.

title: Androlepis skinneri with Dyckia platyphylla
description: A large growing landscape type bromeliad with beautifully colored coppery-bronze foliage when grown in full sun.  I have yet to fully determine whether this is hardy enough to grow outdoors year round in California, as the specimen shown here came straight from southern Floridan into the cooler: it was planted out in the dead of winter, not the best way to acclimate any bromeliad coming from a warmer climate.  This one did survive the winter, but didn't seem to much like the cold.  Another I planted in the Oakland hills exposed to the winter rains, went into a slow decline and rotted out by the time April rolled around.  I intend to try again, but with a bit more protection in the winter, perhaps an enclosed porch or cabana would better suit it.

title: 28 Vallejo St. Rear Garden with paving detail
description: View down into garden from 3rd story deck off kitchen.  The hardscape was intended as a sculptural component of the garden and a play on the theme of squares as developed within the house and in the garden at varying scales.  Indonesian smooth turquoise pebbles were used as an inlay detail between the concrete pads.  Three species of palm are visible in the shot, the blue palm is Brahea 'Clara', the palm at wall to stairs is Arenga engleri, and foliage at right is Trachycarpus fortunei.

title: Palm as accent
description: This silver foliaged palm is an excellent, larger sized and faster growing alternative to the more familiar Brahea armata, which is also beautiful, but so much slower in cool climate conditions.  Of course, when any palm has foliage this beautiful, maybe you don't want it to get tall too fast, but this natural occurring hybrid, Brahea 'Clara' is more adapted to cooler summer climates.  It is a hybrid between Brahea armata and B. brandegeana, and has longer stems on the fronds, plus a more weeping effect to the foliage.  Shown here with an understory planting of Aeoniums and bromeliads, and a hybrid  New Zealand  Clematis 'Avalanche' against the white stucco wall.

title: Greenovia aurea
description: A very cool cousin of the Aeoniums, but with a distinctively different growth habit.  Makes a superb specimen accent plant for containers, as seed here.  Most often monocarpic,(dies after blooming), but can sometimes give offsets.

title: Mahonia lomariifolia foliage with Kentia palm
Decorative screening wall and planter at main terrace
Container plantings with a difference...
description: These plants all together are probably an "only in California" mix of plants.  We have the mild year round climate to keep all these plants happy.  Included here are Anigozanthus flavidus, Lobularia maritima, Graptoveria 'Fred Ives', Linaria reticulata 'Flamingo',  Banksia blechnifolia, Diplandenia splendens 'Red Riding Hood', Alyogyne huegelii in the same raised planter.  The mix of deep red, magenta, purple, lilac with the soft green fern-like foliage of the Banksia make for such great contrasts with the redwood  and live oak tree backdrop.  This terrace felt like an island of color within the forest, up in the tree tops.

title: Stairs, inlay pebble detail, jacuzzi and palms
Brahea 'Clara' as sculpture
description: Definitely a palm that functions well as an accent feature while young, with dramatic weeping silvery foliage that gently sway in the breeze.

title: View from the bathroom at entry
description: Container with Violas and Farfugium japonicum 'aureo-maculata' and Monstera deliciosa.  Note that the spotted leaves repeat the spots on the pot detail, but with reverse light values.  I also chose this variegated foliage to lighten up a dark entry, and play off the dappled shadows the Live Oak tree casts upon the entry.  The palm fronds and Split-leaf Philodendron continue the mostly all foliage effect at the entry, with their year round good looks.

title: View of lower garden from jacuzzi
Cantilevered balcony off kitchen with hanging garden plants
View of lower garden at stairs
View of main terrace from cantilevered deck at kitchen
description: This view shows how spacious the main terrace off the family room is, with the single remaining original Live Oak tree shading a good portion of the space.

title: 28 Vallejo St Rear Garden with view back to the jacuzzi
description: View from the east end of the garden and the final stopping point/small patio, looking back towards the jacuzzi.  Balinese carved stone lanterns with low voltage lighting and Indonesian turquoise pebble inlay, along with rustic Vietnamese large planting urns with restios give a contemporary and also Asian flavor.  Light colored foliage of the Echeveria elegans and Astelia nivicola 'Red Gem' where chosen as edge plantings to help define the edge in the evening dusk.  Using light or silver colored foliage at the edges of paths is a useful design trick to increase visibility of walks in dim light conditions.

title: Brahea 'Clara' palm at lower garden
description: This palm species was chosen to act as a focal point for the lowest level of the garden, and provide ultimate contrast to all the predominant greens.  The alternating materials of the rear fence and wall were selected to help tie the garden to the architecture of the house, and introduce one more layer of rhythm to the garden, continuing on the theme of squares and rectangles used throughout the house and gardens.

title: Salvia splendens 'Van Houttii', a personal favorite
description: If you are also a fan of vivid luscious red flowers, this is one Salvia you should seek out.  Who would believe that the bedding Salvia splendens cultivars that are planted out at municipal parks and gas stations across the country are any relation to this form?  In parts of the country that see no real winter frost, this can easily get 8 feet tall, and have 100's of flowers at the same time, over 9 months of the year here in Berkeley.  I particularly love the subtle contrast between the more burgundy red calyx and lighter red petals.  It also makes a fabulous bouquet for an over the top floral arrangement.  Not to mention that it is also very popular with hummingbirds in the garden.

title: Grasses, Bamboo and Acanthus
description:
This  vignette is all about the foliage color and texture, with just a hint of bloom seasonally.  I like the complementary foliage texture of the Mexican Weeping Bamboo, Otataea acuminata v. aztectorum with the similarly weeping Stipa arundinacea, which colors up orange and rust as it get a bit older.  The dark green glossy foliage of the Bear's Breech, Acanthus spinosissimus gives a sculptural accent at the end of the bench, also contrasting with the softly opalescent silver and lavender tones of the succulent Graptoveria 'Fred Ives' below it.  The Acanthus flowers are also a good color complement to the Graptoveria foliage.  Against the grape stake wood fence, is a late summer blooming Orange Ginger, Hedychium greenii, and a winter blooming Hardenbergia violacea 'Canoelands', which is a mass of purple from November into April.  The sottly lime green ground cover, Sedum palmeri is an explosion of acid yellow flowers in early spring, but I think I actually prefer it as seen here, just quietly elegant.

The mass of the poured concrete anchors the setting, as well as allowing one to enjoy it up close.  It also serves a practical concern, as it was necessary to allow filling in with some soil for plantings over solid rock in this portion of the garden.  Built-in benches can be a useful design tool to save space in small compact gardens; they allow seating without the clutter of furniture, and certainly are easier to maintain.

title: 28 Vallejo St, Built-in planter at deck off kitchen
description: Lots of color in winter and summer in this shot from the annual Linaria reticulata(the only South African plant in this mix), along with Lobularia maritima, two color forms of Anigozanthus hybrids and pale new expanding leaves of Banksia blechnifolia.  All the color in these raised planters really popped against  the pure white stuccoed walls and greens of the trees below.  The intent of these colorful plantings was to contrast with the mid ground views of the deep greens of the surrounding canyon filled with Coast Live Oaks, and the distant glimpse of a view of San Francisco Bay and the city.  I especially like the subtle color harmony of the new Banksia foliage and the flowers.

title: 28 Vallejo St Kitchen Deck planter vignette
28 Vallejo St Front Entry garden walk
description: This view is looking from the front entry porch back towards the street, showing the decorative entry portal with metal gate and etched glass inset panels screening the entry and courtyard from street view.

title: Timeless Foliage texture
description: This combination of greens on greens showcases texture and form over flowers at this moment, but the Mahonia lomariifolia has brilliantly colorful bright yellow flowers in winter and showy blue berries in spring, and the back drop of the clumping Blue Stem Bamboo, Himalayacalamus  hookerianum 'Bill Teague' at the fence has intensely blue stems, and will grow 20 tall to give complete screening from the neighbors in a few years.  The stripped trunk of this Windmill Palm, Trachycarpus fortunei has fantastic ringed green/blue trunks.  Flowering understory plants include a pale yellow  Abutilon behind the palm,  a ground cover of pale orange/pink flowered Veltheimia bracteata, with the high gloss leaves of  Angelica pachycarpa  by the  seat wall.

title: Brahea 'Clara' with Portea 'Jungles'
description: This palm has extra elegance from the long weeping tips of each frond.

title: Dyckia 'Cactus Ranch Red' and Echeveria elegans
Strobilanthes dyeranus
description: This is usually considered a tender tropical for a summer annual in our part of the Bay Area, but it can easily keep going if used as a container plant on a covered porch, which seems to give it just enough of a boost in temperatures to keep looking this good all winter.  Left outdoors unprotected, unfortunately... not so much, at least in my garden, where it just kind of melts by the end of January.  Unfair really, as it is a very reliable return from the roots sort of herbaceous perennial in hotter summer climates.

title: 28 Vallejo ST rear garden curving stairs
description: Garden access as sculpture and experience.  The stairs take you straight to the jacuzzi, which is positioned to give views back up towards the house as well as of the lower garden level.

title: Raised planter at middle terrace below live oak tree
Aechmea caudata and Arctotis 'Burgundy'
description: An intermediate sized rosette form of Aechmea caudata with foliage that tops out at about 20 inches tall rather than 3 feet tall as for the larger forms I also grow.  This particular clone has very pronounced branching of the inflorescence, and typically blooms in mid spring into early summer with these arching inflorescences.

title: View of terrace from family room
Geometry in the garden
description: The overhead view of the Brahea 'Clara' palm is as beautiful as a profile or head on view, and is the focal point view when looking down on this end of the garden from the mid level terrace.

title: Cannomois grandis
description: This restio was chosen to give some additional light screening against the lower property line fence, as the stems can get 8 feet tall, and have wonderful feathery pale olive green foliage as well.  The large Vietnamese urns were chosen for their earthy texture and color, and to provide addtional height from the start for the restios.
